correctness.rationale: For a two-dimensional subcode attaining \(d_2\), doubly-evenness forces each of the three nonzero binary projective column multiplicities to be even. Splitting each class exactly in half, a hypothetical \(d_2\ge2R_2+2\) makes both pieces in the covering decomposition have support below \(d_2\), hence rank one. The resulting rank-one idempotent can make at most half the minimum-support columns vanish, forcing covering distance at least \(d_2/2\ge R_2+1\), a contradiction. Thus \(d_2\le2R_2+1\); parity makes \(d_2\) even and gives \(d_2\le2R_2\). The finite verifier checks small cases but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Doubly-even codes form a standard and mathematically motivated binary class. The theorem gives a uniform strict generalized packing--covering gap at order two, rather than a finite parameter computation, and isolates a structural mechanism—divisibility forcing exact parity of projective multiplicities—that can inform further work on divisible-code covering problems.
